newsitem.title: CUBA: Cuba welcomes Rio Group criticism of U.S. law.
newsitem.headline: Cuba welcomes Rio Group criticism of U.S. law.

text.p: Cuba on Thursday welcomed the stand of the Rio Group of 14 Latin American states condemning U.S. legislation aimed at curbing foreign investment on the Caribbean island.
"We are pleased with this decision, which does not come as a surprise," Cuban Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Marianela Ferriol told a weekly news briefing in Havana.
Rio Group leaders in Cochabamba, Bolivia, this week condemned the so-called Helms-Burton law passed in March in retaliation for Cuba's shooting down of two small U.S. planes.

The U.S. law, which tightens an existing U.S. economic embargo on communist-ruled Cuba, threatens penalties against foreign firms and their executives who "traffick" in confiscated property on the island formerly owned by U.S. nationals or Cubans who later took U.S. citizenship.
The law has drawn strong international criticism including from the European Union, which is drafting retaliatory measures of its own.
